If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

The issue is with the `org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarArchiveInputStream.parsePaxHeaders()` method. The method is responsible for parsing PAX headers from an input stream. The problem occurs when there is an empty line at the end of the headers, leading to a `NegativeArraySizeException`.

The method reads the length of the header but encounters a newline character instead of a digit. This newline character causes the calculation of a negative length, which leads to an attempt to allocate a negative-sized array.

To fix this issue, a check should be added to ensure that the character `ch` is a digit before calculating the length. This will prevent the negative length calculation and the subsequent exception.

Next, I will provide a step-by-step diagnosis based on the available information.
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The current bug report describes that the `TarArchiveInputStream.parsePaxHeaders` method fails with a `NegativeArraySizeException` when there is an empty line at the end of the headers. The issue stems from the method attempting to calculate the length of the header without verifying the character type. When encountering a newline character instead of a digit, the method incorrectly calculates a negative length, leading to the exception when trying to allocate an array.

1. The `TarArchiveInputStream.parsePaxHeaders` method reads the length of the header in an inner loop.
2. When the loop encounters a character that is not a digit, specifically a newline character, it uses that character to calculate the length.
3. The calculation results in a negative length, causing the method to attempt to allocate a negative-sized array, which triggers the `NegativeArraySizeException`.

This issue can be resolved by adding a check to ensure that the character `ch` is a digit before calculating the length to prevent the negative length calculation.

The recent bug reports do not provide direct relevance to this specific issue. Therefore, the focus should be on fixing the calculation of the header length in the `TarArchiveInputStream.parsePaxHeaders` method.

Suggested methods to fix:
```
org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarArchiveInputStream.parsePaxHeaders(java.io.InputStream)
```

Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
